Cc: Ben Carter <ben_carter@redwood.com>, Irene Choi <irene_choi@redwood.com>

Subject: Airlock qualification recap & runbook asks

Hi Sophie — thanks again for taking the time to walk through Echelon's hosting constraints this morning. Quick recap from our side and a short list of asks so we can size the Private/VPC path and draft a focused runbook.

Summary of pain & goals (what we heard)
- Regulatory driver: clinical trial data (PHI + device telemetry) must remain within customer-managed network and cannot traverse public internet egress.
- Desired model residency: on-prem or VPC with strict outbound controls (no direct internet egress from inference nodes).
- Air-gap preference for certain environments: ability to patch and update via an "airlock" jumpbox under customer control; limited manual sync windows.
- Ops constraint: narrow maintenance windows (2 hrs monthly) and no automated outbound telemetry to third-party monitoring without explicit allowlist.

Technical constraints you confirmed
- Inference nodes will sit in a segregated VLAN with NAT blocked; only an internal jump-host (airlock) can fetch signed artifacts.
- No persistent cloud-hosted KMS; customer will provide HSM/KMS endpoints reachable only from inside their VPC.
- Proxying of model updates must be tenant-controlled (signed manifest + checksum).

Immediate asks / next artifacts we need from Echelon
1) Network snapshot (diagram + CIDR ranges, firewall rule examples) — you agreed to share a current diagram.
2) Compliance spreadsheet with required evidence types (SOC2 sections in-scope, controls for data-in-transit/at-rest).
3) Contact for your infra owner who will perform the port/IP allowlist test.

What Redwood will deliver next week
- A 1-page runbook draft describing the airlock flow for model updates, artifact signing, and rollback steps.
- A minimal SOW-ready bulleted checklist for your legal/procurement team that captures required commitments.
- A tentative plan for a 90-minute technical deep-dive (network + ops) to validate NAT/route behavior and HSM connectivity.

Attachments: airlock-network-snapshot.pdf (placeholder — please replace with your network diagram), echelon-compliance-asks.xlsx (we've attached our template to map controls).

Proposed next steps
- Sophie to send network diagram + compliance spreadsheet by EOD Wednesday (Nov 4).
- Redwood to send runbook draft by Nov 6 and propose times for the technical deep-dive (week of Nov 9).

If any item above is off, flag it and I'll adjust. Otherwise we'll treat this as the baseline for scoping the Private deployment.

Thanks —
Mina Haddad
Enterprise Solutions
Redwood Inference

Thanks Mina — appreciate the clear recap. Quick clarifications from our side:
- We'll send the network diagram (including VLANs and NAT rules) by EOD Wednesday — I'll include our infra lead, David Park, in that email.
- For HSM: we use an on-prem HSM (Thales) with an enterprise gateway; we can provide connectivity docs but cannot expose a cloud-managed KMS endpoint.
- Airlock flow: yes, we'd prefer signed manifests + a scheduled manual pull from the jumpbox (no outbound requests from the inference hosts).

One small ask: can Redwood confirm whether the runtime requires outbound telemetry during inference (call-home) by default? If so, we need the option to disable or allowlist only specific internal endpoints.

I'll get the diagram and the compliance spreadsheet to you tomorrow.

Sophie

Sophie — thanks for the quick reply. Short answers to your question in-line below and a proposed timing for a technical workshop.

> "Can Redwood confirm whether the runtime requires outbound telemetry during inference (call-home) by default?"
- Redwood runtime has optional telemetry but it is configurable per deployment. For Private/VPC we can ship with telemetry disabled by default; we will provide an allowlist mode where telemetry may be routed only to customer-managed collectors in your network.

Proposed technical deep-dive (90 minutes)
- Participants: David Park (Echelon infra), Sophie Kern, Mina, Ben, Redwood infra engineer (Irene), and our security lead (TBD).
- Agenda: 1) Walk network diagram and firewall rules; 2) Validate HSM connectivity using our checklist; 3) Demonstrate airlock artifact flow with demo manifests; 4) Confirm telemetry and logging knobs.
- Dates we can offer: Nov 10 (10:00–11:30 PT), Nov 11 (13:00–14:30 PT), Nov 12 (09:00–10:30 PT). Please confirm David's availability and preferred slot.

I'll assemble a short workshop checklist and send it after we get the diagram.
